test_name: RE-friction unsigned-byte-vm-selector exact fixture, acceptance, and two-pass stage control
inspiration: upstream JumpTable signed-label contract; RE-friction need unsigned-byte-vm-selector on KataVM_L1 0x12d0
decisions: Required range opcodes prove signedness, and transparent ZEXT/SEXT paths independently prove the underlying selector unsigned/signed; all evidence must agree.
Equality constants never vote, but widened constants are safely projected to the canonical selector width and conflicting or ambiguous paths decline recovery.

A shrinking zero-offset SUBPIECE declines strict recovery because the address-only restart record cannot preserve the projection; same-width SUBPIECE remains transparent, while option off retains the historical peel to the wider input.
The proven bit is stored in the restart-surviving lowered-switch record and installed directly on the synthetic JumpTable.
The generic numeric printer is unchanged; explicit option-off ablation bypasses all new proof/decline semantics and retains legacy structural recovery plus the historical case-bit guess.
Default-on remains contingent on zero inherited parity movement and a speed delta within 5%.

controls.positive: exact unsigned-byte 0x8b fixture, signed byte -117, signed int -1, unsigned u32 0xffffffff, matching ZEXT/unsigned and SEXT/signed widened selectors, and widened-constant normalization
controls.negative: ZEXT/signed and SEXT/unsigned range conflicts, mixed ZEXT/SEXT paths, mixed signed/unsigned range cascades, and a live four-byte source projected through a low-byte SUBPIECE decline recovery; the truncation control keeps the ambiguous outer head in the map so no inner subtree recovers, while option-off controls recover the conflicting structures and legacy wide-selector peel
